sources.name: European Commission
sources.text: Report on Greek Government Deficit and Debt Statistics, COM(2010) 1 final, 8 January 2010: the 2008 revision from 5.0% to 7.7% of GDP and the 2009 planned deficit from 3.7% to 12.5%; the 2 notifications of 2 and 21 October 2009; the 22 October 2009 reservation "due to significant uncertainties over the figures notified by the Greek statistical authorities"; the November 2004 report "involving no less than 11 separate issues"; 5 reservations between 2005 and 2009; that clean publication was "very often the result of Eurostat interventions ... with the result of increasing the notified deficit"; specific filings recorded as "a case of deliberate misreporting of figures" by the GAO and the NSSG; and the conclusion that the framework "cannot prevent deliberate misreporting of data" and did not address "institutional settings, accountability, responsibility and political interference." Read as text extracted from the published PDF.

sources.name: Eurostat
sources.text: News Release 55/2010, 22 April 2010: Greece's 2009 deficit at 13.6% of GDP and debt at 115.1%, with a reservation "due to uncertainties on the surplus of social security funds for 2009, on the classification of some public entities and on the recording of off-market swaps" that "could lead to a revision for the year 2009 of the order of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage points of GDP for the deficit and 5 to 7 percentage points of GDP for the debt."

sources.name: Eurostat
sources.text: News Release, 15 November 2010: Greece's 2009 deficit at 15.4% of GDP and debt at 126.8%, and the lifting of the April reservation after "a series of EDP methodological visits." Against the April estimate, the deficit moved 1.8 points and the debt 11.7.

sources.name: Eurostat
sources.text: Report on the revision of the Greek government deficit and debt figures, November 2004: the restatement of 1997 to 6.6% of GDP instead of 4.0%, 1998 to 4.3% instead of 2.5%, and 1999 to 3.4% instead of 1.8%, with debt for the same years restated from 108.2%, 105.8% and 105.2% to 114.0%, 112.4% and 112.3%. Causes given include the recording of military equipment expenditure and of capital injections financed by EU grants.

sources.name: International Statistical Institute
sources.text: Background and chronology of court proceedings against Andreas Georgiou: appointment as ELSTAT president in August 2010 under Law 3832 and retirement in August 2015; the felony charge that the defendants "conspired among themselves, and with international agencies (i.e. Eurostat and the IMF), to artificially inflate the public deficit figures", with alleged damage of €171 billion and later over €200 billion; the 1 August 2017 acquittal on 2 counts and conviction on the count of "not putting up the 2009 EDP figures for approval by the former ELSTAT Board" with a 2-year suspended sentence; the June 2018 Supreme Court decision that "rendered the conviction and prison sentence irreversible"; the April 2019 closure "with the full acquittal of the defendants"; the 2016 defamation conviction and 1-year suspended sentence; and that Eurostat published the revised statistics "lifting all reservations on them" and continued to do so for the following 9 years.
